# Markless docs

> The Markless documentation: build for any device, the web way. Elements and events in TypeScript, with an API designed to compile to any device.

Generated by scripts/generate-seo.ts from nav.ts. Every page below is prose plus
runnable `.tsrx` files, written against @markless/* 0.5.0. Where something
on this site does not work on that version, the page says so out loud in a callout
rather than documenting the plan.

## Start here

- [What is Markless](https://markless.dev/): What Markless is: elements and events in TypeScript, with an API designed to compile to any device. The browser, server rendering and tests work today, and iOS and macOS are early proofs.
- [Creating a new app](https://markless.dev/start/new-app): Make a new app with one command, open it in your browser, and change it.
- [Adding to an existing site](https://markless.dev/start/existing-site): Put a Markless component into one element of an HTML page you already have, with Vite and render(), and ship static files.
- [Reading a .tsrx file](https://markless.dev/start/reading-tsrx): Every part of a .tsrx file, line by line, then the other files in a starter app.

## Core concepts

- [State](https://markless.dev/concepts/state): state() tells the page to watch a variable. You read it and assign to it like any other let.
- [Computed](https://markless.dev/concepts/computed): A value you work out is never out of date. computed() derives one value from others and works it out again when one of them changes.
- [Events](https://markless.dev/concepts/events): An event prop is on plus the DOM event name, and the browser hands your handler its own typed event object.
- [Conditionals](https://markless.dev/concepts/conditionals): @if puts real elements on the page and takes them off again, so a value that must outlive the branch is declared above it.
- [Lists](https://markless.dev/concepts/lists): A key answers the question of which row is which. Once a row has one, its state, its DOM and its event wiring move with it through a sort.
- [Async](https://markless.dev/concepts/async): Waiting is a block, not a flag: @try, @pending and @catch are the whole status vocabulary, so there is no loading boolean to forget.
- [Styling](https://markless.dev/concepts/styling): A style block written inside a component styles that component and nothing else, so two components can both call something .card.

## Building an app

- [Components](https://markless.dev/build/components): A component is a function and props are its parameters, callbacks and children included, with the parent value read through live.
- [Elements](https://markless.dev/build/elements): An element is not state. element() gives you a handle, bound with el, that points at one real element once it is on the page.
- [Storage](https://markless.dev/build/storage): storage() is a variable you read and write like any other, saved in the browser and applied before the first paint.
- [Shared](https://markless.dev/build/shared): shared() gives a piece of data a name, so a component that wants it calls the name instead of having it threaded down through props.

## Router

- [Pages](https://markless.dev/router/pages): A file under pages/ is a URL, brackets in the file name are parameters, and the path on disk is the path in the address bar.
- [Links](https://markless.dev/router/links): Link to a route pattern and pass its params, and the build checks both, so a link with a typo stops the build instead of shipping a 404.
- [Page data](https://markless.dev/router/data): There is no loader: a page loads data with an async computed() inside @try, and the slow part arrives later in the same response.
- [API routes](https://markless.dev/router/api-routes): A file in api/ is an endpoint: the address comes from the path, the HTTP method from the file name, and the file default-exports one function.
- [Deploying](https://markless.dev/router/deploying): Build once into .output/ for a Node server, or pick another host with a Nitro preset. Your files stay the same.

## Tooling

- [Editor setup](https://markless.dev/tooling/editor-setup): An editor extension colours .tsrx files; a TypeScript plugin named in tsconfig.json adds Markless suggestions, hints and errors.
- [Type checking](https://markless.dev/tooling/type-checking): TypeScript checks a TSX copy of each .tsrx file, and every error points back to the line you wrote.
- [Testing](https://markless.dev/tooling/testing): @markless/vitest-browser mounts a component in a real browser or renders it on a test server, and your test clicks it.
- [Diagnostics](https://markless.dev/tooling/diagnostics): Each Markless error names a code, says why, suggests a fix and links to its page; markless-allow silences one warning.

## How it works

- [Design choices](https://markless.dev/how-it-works): The design choices behind Markless on one page, for contributors and agents who want to weigh how it works.
- [The big idea](https://markless.dev/how-it-works/the-big-idea): Markless reads a component at build time instead of running it, so the plan is written before anything renders, anywhere.
- [The compiler](https://markless.dev/how-it-works/compiler): The real output the compiler makes from a counter: its state, its updates and the code each event runs.
- [The payload](https://markless.dev/how-it-works/payload): What a server adds to its HTML so the browser can carry on: the state values, which element does what, and a small script that waits for the first interaction.
- [Resuming](https://markless.dev/how-it-works/resuming): Who hears the first click on each of the three paths a page can take: the browser with a direct module, the browser on the general path, or a server-rendered page.
- [The state graph](https://markless.dev/how-it-works/state-graph): The compiler writes down who reads what before the page exists, so one write touches one text node.
- [Lazy chunks](https://markless.dev/how-it-works/lazy-chunks): Where the small functions behind each handler and update live, and when the browser gets and runs them.
- [Native targets](https://markless.dev/how-it-works/native-targets): The same counter on a phone: the state graph and its functions are data, so a browser is not the only place they run.

## Contributing

- [Repo tour](https://markless.dev/contributing): Where each package lives and its job, from compile time to rendering anywhere.
- [Dev setup](https://markless.dev/contributing/dev-setup): Clone, install with pnpm, and the root scripts you run every day.
- [Your first PR](https://markless.dev/contributing/first-pr): The path from a branch to a merged change, with the checks you run first.
- [CI and checks](https://markless.dev/contributing/ci): What each CI job runs and how pnpm ci:local runs the same commands.
- [Specs and rules](https://markless.dev/contributing/specs-and-rules): Where the behavior contract and contributor rules live.
- [Improve the docs](https://markless.dev/contributing/improve-the-docs): How to fix a page on this site, or add a new one.

- [Packages](https://markless.dev/reference): Every Markless package, what it does, and its npm version.
- [Glossary](https://markless.dev/reference/glossary): One meaning for each word these docs use.
- [CLI](https://markless.dev/reference/cli): The create-markless flags, starters and new-app scripts.
- [Error codes](https://markless.dev/errors): Every MARKLESS_ code Markless can print, grouped by the package that raises it, each with its own page.
